t: Insurance has been described as 'the losses of the few being shared by the many'. This refers to:
e: Pooling collects contributions from many exposed to similar risks so that the losses of the unfortunate few are met from the common fund.

t: Which company, established in Calcutta in 1850, is regarded as the first general insurance company in India?
e: Triton Insurance Company Ltd, set up in 1850 by the British in Calcutta, was the first general insurer in India.

t: A two-wheeler own-damage claim is assessed at Rs 25,000. The policy carries a compulsory excess of Rs 2,000. The amount payable by the insurer is:
e: The excess (deductible) is the first portion of every loss borne by the insured, so the insurer pays 25,000 - 2,000 = Rs 23,000.

t: Three months into a fire policy, the insured shifts his insured stock to a new godown and informs the insurer. The insurer should record this change by issuing a:
e: A mid-term change in location of the insured property is a material alteration recorded through an endorsement to the existing policy.

t: Following the opening up of the insurance sector, the General Insurance Corporation of India was re-designated in the year 2000 as the:
e: In November 2000 GIC was notified as the Indian reinsurer and ceased direct underwriting; its four subsidiaries were later delinked in 2002.

t: Which principle allows an insurer to predict total losses in a pool more accurately as the number of similar exposures increases?
e: The law of large numbers states that actual results approach expected results as the number of independent, homogeneous exposures grows.

t: A storm blows down a compound wall which falls on a parked car and damages it. The proximate cause of the damage to the car is:
e: The storm set in motion an unbroken chain of events ending in the damage, so it is the proximate cause even though the wall was the immediate agent.

t: Which of the following was NOT one of the four subsidiaries of the General Insurance Corporation of India formed under the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972?
o: The New India Assurance Company Ltd
Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India
e: GIBNA 1972 created GIC with four subsidiaries: National, New India, Oriental and United India. ECGC is a separate Government company.

t: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, insurance is treated as:
o: A 'service', so policyholders can approach consumer commissions for deficiency in service
A banking product outside the Act
A matter exclusively for civil courts
e: Insurance is expressly included in the definition of 'service', enabling consumer commissions to hear complaints of deficiency against insurers.

t: Under Section 10 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, which of the following is NOT an essential of a valid contract?
o: The agreement must be in writing
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). A contract need not be written to be valid; the essentials are offer and acceptance, consideration, capacity, free consent and lawful object.

t: Under current IRDAI norms, an individual insurance agent may represent at most:
o: One life insurer, one general insurer and one standalone health insurer
Any number of insurers of each class
Only one insurer of any class
Two life insurers and two general insurers
e: An individual agent may hold a composite appointment with one life, one general and one health insurer (and one each of the mono-line insurers).

t: The principle of subrogation does NOT apply to:
e: Subrogation is a corollary of indemnity; life insurance is not a contract of indemnity, so the insurer gets no rights against third parties.

t: In life insurance, insurable interest must exist:
o: Only at the time of the claim
At the time the contract is taken
Both at inception and at the time of death
e: For life insurance the interest need exist only at inception; the policy remains valid even if the relationship later ends, e.g., after divorce.

t: The grace period for payment of renewal premium under a life insurance policy with yearly, half-yearly or quarterly premium mode is normally:
e: Life policies allow a grace period of 30 days (one month) for annual, half-yearly and quarterly modes, and 15 days for the monthly mode.

t: The Insurance Institute of India, which conducts the Licentiate, Associateship and Fellowship examinations, was established in 1955 with its headquarters in:
e: The Insurance Institute of India (formerly Federation of Insurance Institutes) was set up in 1955 and is headquartered in Mumbai.

t: A textile mill installs automatic sprinklers and fire alarms in its godown. Which risk management technique is being used?
e: Measures that reduce the frequency or severity of loss without giving up the activity are loss reduction or risk control measures.

t: The Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act, 2015 raised the permissible foreign investment limit in Indian insurance companies from 26% to:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The 2015 amendment increased the composite foreign investment cap from 26% to 49%, with Indian ownership and control.

t: Under IRDAI regulations, appointment of a licensed surveyor for assessing a general insurance loss (other than motor) is required when the claim amount exceeds:
e: IRDAI's Protection of Policyholders' Interests Regulations require a licensed surveyor for motor claims above Rs 50,000 and other claims above Rs 1 lakh.

t: Under the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act, 2015, the minimum paid-up equity capital required to carry on exclusively health insurance business in India is:
e: The 2015 amendment recognised health insurance as a separate class and prescribed a minimum paid-up capital of Rs 100 crore for a standalone health insurer.

t: If a proposer fails to disclose a material fact, the contract of insurance becomes:
o: Voidable at the option of the insurer
Voidable at the option of the insured
e: Breach of utmost good faith makes the contract voidable; the innocent party, usually the insurer, may elect to avoid it.

t: Under co-insurance, as understood in Indian general insurance practice:
o: The insured bears a fixed percentage of every claim
Two or more insurers share a large risk directly with the insured, each liable for its agreed percentage, with one acting as leader
The insurer passes the whole risk to a reinsurer
The policy is issued jointly in the names of husband and wife
e: Co-insurance divides a single risk among several direct insurers in agreed shares; the leading insurer issues the policy and services the claim.

t: Which of the following is NOT normally a rating factor for private car own-damage premium in India?
e: Motor own-damage rating depends on insured's declared value, cubic capacity, age and zone; colour has no bearing on the risk.

t: Insurable interest means that the insured must:
o: Stand to suffer a financial loss if the insured event occurs
Own the subject matter outright in all cases
Have paid at least one full year's premium
e: Insurable interest is a legally recognised financial relationship with the subject matter such that the insured benefits from its safety and is prejudiced by its loss.

t: A fire that destroys a factory building is, in insurance terminology, an example of a:
e: A peril is the actual cause of a loss; a hazard is a condition that increases the chance or severity of loss from a peril.

t: Which of the following is NOT a benefit that insurance provides to society?
o: Mobilisation of savings for long-term investment
Financial security and peace of mind
Elimination of all perils such as fire and flood
e: Insurance compensates the financial consequences of perils but cannot prevent or eliminate the perils themselves.

t: Reinsurance arranged individually for a single risk, where the reinsurer is free to accept or decline each offer, is called:
e: Facultative reinsurance is negotiated case by case; under a treaty the reinsurer must accept all risks falling within agreed limits.

t: Under Section 30 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, which type of agreement is declared void?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Wagering agreements are void; insurance is distinguished from a wager by the presence of insurable interest.

t: A godown worth Rs 20 lakh is insured for Rs 10 lakh under a fire policy subject to average. A fire causes damage of Rs 4 lakh. How much will the insurer pay?
e: Under the average clause, claim = loss x (sum insured / value) = 4 x 10/20 = Rs 2 lakh, as the insured is treated as his own insurer for the balance.

t: Premium is:
o: The consideration paid by the insured to the insurer for the risk undertaken
The amount paid by the insurer on a claim
The commission paid to the agent
e: Premium is the price of insurance paid by the insured; it is the insured's consideration for the insurer's promise.

t: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, which created the insurance regulator, was passed by Parliament in:
e: The IRDA Act was enacted in December 1999 and the Authority was constituted as a statutory body in April 2000.

t: An agent offers to return part of his commission to a customer as an inducement to buy a policy. This practice is prohibited under which section of the Insurance Act, 1938?
e: Section 41 prohibits rebating of premium or commission as an inducement to take or renew insurance and prescribes a penalty.

t: On the death of a life assured who had validly nominated his wife under Section 39 of the Insurance Act, the insurer pays the death claim to:
o: All legal heirs in equal shares
The agent who sold the policy
e: A valid nomination entitles the nominee to receive the policy money, giving the insurer a good discharge; the 2015 amendment made close-relative nominees beneficial owners.

t: An endowment assurance policy pays the sum assured:
o: On death during the term or on survival to the end of the term, whichever is earlier
Only on death during the term
Only on survival to the end of the term
e: Endowment combines protection and savings: the sum assured is paid on death within the term or on maturity if the life assured survives.

t: Which of the following is a speculative risk?
o: Fire damage to a dwelling house
Theft of jewellery from a locker
e: Speculative risks carry the possibility of gain as well as loss (e.g., investment), whereas pure risks involve only loss or no loss.

t: A 17-year-old student signs a proposal form and pays premium for a policy in his own name. Under the Indian Contract Act, the agreement is:
o: Void, as a minor is not competent to contract
e: Section 11 requires parties to have attained majority; an agreement with a minor is void ab initio.

t: A critical illness policy that pays a fixed lump sum on diagnosis of a specified disease, irrespective of actual medical expenses, is a:
e: Fixed benefit covers pay a pre-agreed amount on occurrence of the event, unlike indemnity-based mediclaim which reimburses actual expenses.

t: The essential difference between nomination and assignment of a life policy is that:
o: Nomination can be made only at inception while assignment can be made any time
Assignment transfers the rights and title in the policy to the assignee, whereas nomination merely names the person to receive the money on death
Nomination requires the insurer's consent while assignment does not
There is no difference between the two
e: Assignment (Section 38) transfers ownership of the policy; nomination (Section 39) only designates who receives the proceeds and does not transfer title.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required to start a life or general insurance company in India is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹100 crore for a direct insurer; ₹200 crore for a reinsurer (Section 6 of the Insurance Act).

t: Which section of the Insurance Act, 1938 requires that premium be received in advance before an insurer assumes any risk?
e: Section 64VB lays down the 'no risk without premium' rule, so cover commences only after the premium is received by the insurer.

t: The main purpose of the proposal form is to:
o: Serve as the receipt for premium paid
Provide the insurer with information needed to assess the risk and form the basis of the contract
Confirm that the claim has been settled
e: The proposal form collects material information about the risk and contains the proposer's declaration of truth, which becomes the basis of the contract.

t: A complaint to the Insurance Ombudsman must ordinarily be made within what period after the insurer has rejected the representation or failed to reply?
e: The Ombudsman Rules require the complaint to be filed within one year of the insurer's rejection, final reply or the expiry of the one-month reply period.

t: An earthquake that damages thousands of homes across a whole district is an example of a:
e: Fundamental risks are impersonal in origin and affect large groups or whole communities, unlike particular risks which affect individuals.

t: After buying comprehensive motor insurance, Suresh stops bothering to lock his car because 'the insurer will pay anyway'. His attitude illustrates:
e: Morale hazard is carelessness or indifference to loss arising from the existence of insurance, as distinct from moral hazard which involves dishonesty.

t: On the occurrence of a loss, the first duty of the insured under a general insurance policy is to:
o: Intimate the insurer promptly, giving particulars of the loss
Repair the damage and then claim
e: Prompt notice enables the insurer to investigate and appoint a surveyor while evidence is fresh; delay may prejudice the claim.

t: Arrange the following in correct chronological order: LIC Act, Insurance Act, IRDA Act, GIBNA.
o: Insurance Act - LIC Act - GIBNA - IRDA Act
LIC Act - Insurance Act - GIBNA - IRDA Act
Insurance Act - GIBNA - LIC Act - IRDA Act
GIBNA - LIC Act - Insurance Act - IRDA Act
e: The Insurance Act came in 1938, the LIC Act in 1956, GIBNA in 1972 and the IRDA Act in 1999.

t: The control level of solvency ratio that every insurer must maintain is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Available solvency margin must be at least 150% of the required solvency margin; falling below triggers IRDAI action.

t: The purpose of a renewal notice sent by a general insurer is to:
o: Legally bind the insured to renew
Remind the insured that the policy is about to expire and invite renewal
Record a change in the sum insured
e: A renewal notice is a courtesy reminder of expiry date and renewal premium; it does not itself create or extend the contract.

t: The Latin term 'uberrima fides' refers to the principle of:
e: Uberrima fides means utmost good faith, the duty on both parties to disclose all material facts fully and truthfully.

t: A stock of goods is insured with Insurer A for Rs 6 lakh and Insurer B for Rs 4 lakh under identical policies. A loss of Rs 2 lakh occurs. On a rateable proportion basis, Insurer A's share is:
e: A's share = loss x (A's sum insured / total sum insured) = 2 x 6/10 = Rs 1.2 lakh; B pays the balance Rs 80,000.

t: Ramesh takes a fire policy on his neighbour Dinesh's house without any financial stake in it. The house burns down. The claim is:
o: Payable to Dinesh under Ramesh's policy
Payable at 50% to each of them
Not payable, as Ramesh has no insurable interest
e: Without insurable interest the contract is a wager and void, so no claim is payable under it.
